defects.title: The lower bound set is 1e4 times the highest uptake rate
defects.trigger: createModel EX_a/EX_b/EX_c (bounds -10..10) + R1 + DM_d with metInChIString; mediaConstraints(model, [-2 -3; 1 4; -1 5], {'InChI=a'; 'InChI=c'; 'InChI=z'}, {'nameA'; 'nameC'; 'nameZ'})
defects.observed: lb(EX_a) = -30000 for uptake rates -2 and -3: line 37 multiplies min(min(Rates(i,:)), 0) by 1e4 (R2025a, 2026-11-23)
defects.expected: lb(EX_a) = -3, the highest uptake rate as the lower bound (help text; original text: 'sets this value as a lower boundary')

notes: Tier 2 in the test header: no solver is used (the ledger says 3). Reproduction: model = createModel({'EX_a','EX_b','EX_c','R1','DM_d'}, {'a','b','c','d','e'}, {' a[e] <=> ',' b[e] <=> ',' c[e] <=> ','a[e] + b[e] -> c[e] + d[c]','d[c] -> '}, 'lowerBoundList', [-10 -10 -10 0 0], 'upperBoundList', [10 10 10 10 10]); model.metInChIString = {'InChI=a'; 'InChI=b'; 'InChI=c'; 'InChI=d'}; [m2, un, upd] = mediaConstraints(model, [-2 -3; 1 4; -1 5], {'InChI=a'; 'InChI=c'; 'InChI=z'}, {'nameA'; 'nameC'; 'nameZ'}) -> m2.lb(1) = -30000, m2.lb(3) = 0 (secretion only, correct), un = {'nameZ'}, upd = {'EX_a'; 'EX_c'}. The 1e4 factor may be a deliberate unit conversion, but it is documented nowhere (the help text even gives mmol/gDW/h); classified wrong-result per the T009a rule (header documents a result the code does not deliver). No src caller: seed NONE. Also: a model without metInChIString errors at line 33 (field not documented; not recorded).
confirmed_by: lead (read the code: the help gives rates in mmol/gDW/h and line 37 sets the lower bound to min(rate,0)*1e4, a factor the help does not mention; no src caller)

defects.trigger: lm.S = sparse([1 -1 0 0; 0 1 -1 -1]); lm.mets = {'A';'B'}; lm.lb = [1;0;0;0]; lm.ub = [10;10;10;10]; lm.N = null(full(lm.S)); [A, b_L, b_U] = defineLinearConstraints(lm, 2)
defects.observed: size(A) = [2 4], b_L = [1 1e-4], b_U = [10 10] (first m reaction bounds: line 163 masks the m rows of S, lines 164-165 apply it to the n bounds); with m > n (S = sparse([1 -1; 1 -1; 1 -1])) MATLAB:badsubscript at line 164 (R2025a, gurobi, 2026-11-23)

defects.title: The reactions given an offset bound depend on the LP solver's feasible point
defects.trigger: lm as above; [A, b_L, b_U] = defineLinearConstraints(lm) (gurobi)
defects.observed: b_L = [1 1e-4 0 1e-4]: reaction 4 gets the 1e-4 bound and reaction 3 does not, although both export B with identical columns and bounds and neither is forced away from zero; the first iteration has a zero objective (lines 118-119, nothing marked) and lines 131-133 mark whatever the returned point uses
defects.expected: the offset only for reactions forced away from zero (help text): b_L = [1 1e-4 0 0]; in any reading reactions 3 and 4 treated alike, independent of the solver

notes: Reach: the method-2 defect is used by no caller (C13ConfidenceInterval passes one argument; fitC13Data sets method = 1 locally, its method-2 branch is unreachable). The second defect is reached by every call with the default method 1: C13ConfidenceInterval.m:123 (PENDING) and fitC13Data.m:59, and fitC13Data already has test/verifiedTests/dataIntegration/testFitC13Data/testFitC13Data.m (lead decision, see final message). Other findings (not recorded as defects): line 36 reads model.N for every method, so a model without N errors (MATLAB:nonExistentField) even for method 2 and the fallback null(model.S) at line 155 is unreachable (N is listed as a model field, so treated as limitation, not entered); an infeasible LP makes lines 124-126 print and call pause (interactive). A model where zero flux is feasible (S = [1 -1], lb 0, ub 10) marks nothing (b_L = [0 0]); a chain forced by lb(1) = 1 gives b_L = [1 1e-4 1e-4] as documented. Reproduction script lines are in the header TRIGGER fields.
confirmed_by: lead (read the code: method 2 builds b_L and b_U per reaction and filters them with a mask over the rows of S, lines 158-165; method 1: line 119 sets the objective of every unmarked reaction to zero, so the first LP has a zero objective and lines 131-133 mark whatever reactions the returned point uses, so identical reactions are treated differently; default seed: every default call (method 1) reaches it, C13ConfidenceInterval among the ledger rows; fitC13Data has a pre-existing test outside the ledger)

notes: Full coverage with gurobi and glpk (glpk runs first in solvers.LP). Line 173 (V = NaN) is reached only with gurobi, which returns an empty solution vector for the infeasible problem; glpk returns its last iterate (9 entries, stat 0), so the NaN check is gurobi-only. In fixed-scaling mode V is the solution of the 1e4-scaled problem (A*V = 1e4*b), in adaptive mode it is unscaled: original FASTCORE design (findSparseMode only thresholds the support), not recorded as a defect. Contrast for LP10weighted: LP10(2, 1, [1;1], LPp, 1e-4, 0, []) on LPp.A = [1 -1; 1 0], b = [0; 1] returns V = [1e4 1e4] (optimal) with gurobi.
